title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 3 and 4.
This question paper consists of 4 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.

questions.prompt: The word 'democracy' comes from Greek. What does 'demos' mean?
From what age can you register as a voter?
Which organisation runs elections in South Africa? (abbreviation)
The Constitution protects the right to protest peacefully and unarmed.
The RCL is…
options: a learners' representative council at school

questions.prompt: Describe THREE ways in which a Grade 9 learner can participate in democracy.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): join/vote for the RCL; sign petitions; peaceful protest; contact the ward councillor; volunteer; register at 16 to vote later; stay informed

questions.prompt: Why is it wrong to burn a library during a protest about service delivery?
questions.memo:
✓ It is a crime and the protest is no longer peaceful (1)
✓ It destroys a service the community needs, harming the people it was meant to help (1)

questions.prompt: Match each election-related term to its meaning.
When the media expose corruption, they are playing which role?
What is the permanent record of your online activity called?
Setting your social media accounts to private helps to protect your safety.
Which South African law makes certain online harms, such as sharing intimate images without consent, a crime?
Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Adult gaining a child's trust to exploit them
Trick to steal money or information

questions.prompt: Describe THREE ways to check whether a news story you see online is true.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): check the author/publisher; check the date; look for evidence; compare with other reliable sources; be wary of emotional headlines; reverse image search

questions.prompt: Why should teenagers think carefully about their digital footprint?
questions.memo:
✓ Posts are permanent and can be shared widely (1)
✓ Future employers or universities may see them / they can affect reputation and safety (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 3: Subject Choice and Career Planning

questions.prompt: Which of these is a compulsory subject in Grades 10 to 12?
How many elective subjects must a learner choose in the FET phase?
What does NSFAS stand for?
Most engineering degrees accept Mathematical Literacy instead of Mathematics.
What score do universities calculate from matric marks to decide on admission? (abbreviation)
Match each NSC pass to what it allows you to study.
Give FOUR factors to consider when choosing FET subjects.
questions.memo: Any four (1 each): interests; abilities/marks; career requirements; subjects offered at school; advice from counsellors/teachers; long-term goals

sections.title: QUESTION 4: Study Strategies and Exam Preparation

questions.prompt: Which is an ACTIVE study strategy?
options: Testing yourself without looking at notes

questions.prompt: What is revising a topic several times over days and weeks called? (… practice)
A 'compare' question asks for both similarities and differences.
Using the guideline of about one minute per mark, how many minutes should you spend on a 15-mark question?
Match each question verb to what it asks.

pairs.right: Judge the value and give reasons

questions.prompt: How can a learner use exam results to improve?
questions.memo:
✓ Analyse mistakes to find why marks were lost (1)
✓ Adjust the study plan / practise weak areas (1)

questions.prompt: How does the mark allocation help you answer a question?
questions.memo:
✓ It shows how many points or how much detail is expected (1)
✓ It helps you plan time and avoid writing too much or too little (1)
